predecessors.name: Ottoman Empire
predecessors.text: the Ottoman provinces Britain held after 1918, among them the vilayet of Mosul (occupied 10 November 1918); the mandate was awarded at San Remo on 25 April 1920

successors.name: Iraqi Republic
successors.text: the Republic of Iraq proclaimed after the coup of 14 July 1958

ledger.x: 1921: the Kingdom of Iraq is founded under the British mandate.
2 December 1922: the Uqair protocol creates the Saudi-Iraqi neutral zone.
4 February 1923: Mosul is left out of the Lausanne talks.
1926: Turkey accepts the League's award of Mosul.
May 1941: Britain defeats the Iraqi rising and occupies Iraq.
1947: the British occupation of Iraq ends.

wars.name: Mosul Question
wars.outcome: Mosul was left out of the Lausanne settlement (4 February 1923), the League of Nations allotted the vilayet to Iraq on 16 December 1925 and Turkey assented in the Frontier Treaty of 1926 for 10 percent of the oil royalties.

wars.name: Anglo-Iraqi War
wars.outcome: British victory in four weeks (2-31 May 1941); the rebellion was suppressed and Britain occupied Iraq until 1947.

wars.name: 1948 Arab-Israeli War (Iraqi expeditionary force)
wars.outcome: An Iraqi brigade group crossed the Jordan on 15 May 1948, besieged Gesher, was repulsed and moved into the Samaria triangle (Nablus, Jenin, Tulkarm), where it became stationary; no Iraqi territory changed.

certainty.note: The Mosul vilayet frontier with Turkey was disputed until 1926; the desert frontiers were undefined.

The Turkish frontier follows the Frontier Treaty of 1926 and the Saudi frontier and neutral zone the Uqair protocol of 2 December 1922; the desert frontiers with Transjordan and Syria are approximate, and the Iranian and Kuwaiti frontiers…
